draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Miramar Beach! It sits right where the Mandovi River meets the Arabian Sea, and its name literally means sea-view, though the Portuguese first called it Porta de Gaspar Dias.
draft.hungryLine: There's a popular café near the beach, close to Clube Gaspar de Dias, for a quick bite after your walk.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Stella Maris Chapel is a 7 min walk and the Science Center is about 9 min away.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Walk down to Miramar Beach, just 5 min from here, and watch the river run into the sea.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Miramar Beach hosted the beach volleyball events of the 2014 Lusofonia Games.

spots.name: Miramar Beach
spots.detail: 5 min walk · Panjim's own beach, where the Mandovi meets the sea

spots.name: Stella Maris Chapel
spots.detail: 7 min walk · A small chapel close to the beach

spots.name: Science Center
spots.detail: 9 min walk · An easy stop near the beach

tips.title: Expect company on the sand.
tips.body: Miramar is one of the most visited beaches in Goa and lots of people come every single day.

tips.title: See what's on at Kala Academy.
tips.body: The Kala Academy at nearby Campal promotes music, dance, drama and folk art, and its building was designed by Charles Correa.

story.title: Porta de Gaspar Dias
story.body: The Portuguese originally named this stretch Porta de Gaspar Dias. Later it became Miramar, from the Spanish and Portuguese for sea-view.

story.title: St Inez Creek
story.body: The nearby Santa Inês creek runs 3.7 km into the Mandovi. A Portuguese plaque dates it to 1829, but historian Percival Noronha traces it back to 1647.

story.title: A home for the arts
story.body: The Government of Goa set up the Kala Academy at Campal on 28 February 1970 to promote music, dance, drama and literature.

story.title: Games on the beach
story.body: Miramar Beach was the venue for beach volleyball at the 2014 Lusofonia Games. Today it is one of only two beaches in Panjim, the other being Caranzalem.
